A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer in-context filtering study. Their complete texts, equations, figures and appendices support comparison; v1's Dual Kalman filtering and control-input appendices are retained in v2 as Appendices B–D.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original simulations of state estimation and output prediction, including missing parameters, vector measurements and control inputs.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices D–F report original linear and nonlinear filtering experiments, target tracking, capacity studies, distribution shifts and multi-step prediction.

M1.justification: The GPT-2 predictor, squared-error training objective and core Kalman-filter construction remain. Appendix E.4 adds recursive feedback of predicted outputs for multi-step inference, a limited extension of v1's one-step procedure.

E1.justification: V2 retains the linear experiments, including control inputs, and adds nonlinear state dynamics, maneuvering-target tracking with nonlinear observations, distribution-shift scenarios and multi-step forecasting. Section 4.3 and Appendices E–F substantially broaden the evaluated task and system coverage.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates Kalman filtering, SGD, ridge regression and OLS. V2 introduces evaluated Extended Kalman Filter and particle-filter baselines for nonlinear systems. Figure 7 also plots SGD, despite the accompanying text saying SGD was omitted.

E3.justification: The stated linear-experiment model changes from 16 to 32 layers, and v2 adds ground-truth MSE alongside MSPD. New protocols include dimension-2 missing-parameter tests, capacity sweeps and recursive forecasting with a fixed future measurement matrix. Ridge settings are inconsistent: Section 4.2 states 0.05, whereas Appendix E.3 states 0.01.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's missing-parameter tests, v2 adds depth and embedding-dimension ablations, state-dimension sensitivity, distribution-shift tests, a reported baseline-parameter sweep, and horizon/noise sensitivity analyses. Tables 1–2 and Appendix E substantially expand the investigation of capacity and robustness.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The 5,000-example evaluation batch is retained; the additional results do not introduce uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: V2 adds MSE results, nonlinear and forecasting results, and capacity tables. Table 1 reports EKF MSPD of 1.0281 with one layer and 0.0526 with eight layers. Figure 5 now distinguishes SGD-like behavior at state dimension 8 from Kalman-like behavior at dimension 2. Revised linear curves use changed model depth, preventing same-setting performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds EKF recursions, nonlinear-system Jacobians and GeLU/Taylor approximation arguments beyond v1's KF/DKF treatment. Appendix G supplies an explicit RAW construction. The new tracking measurement Jacobian contains an incorrect sign: the derivative of arctan(b/a) with respect to b is printed as negative a/(a²+b²).

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary and conclusion expand the central claim from linear Kalman-filter emulation to filtering across linear and nonlinear systems, including EKF/PF comparisons and capacity-dependent behavior. Explicit latent-state recovery becomes preliminary supporting evidence, and missing-parameter robustness receives stronger qualifications.

C2.justification: V2 ties missing-parameter robustness to state dimension and model capacity, qualifying v1's broad interpretation. It additionally attributes regression-error peaks to double descent, long-context plateaus to architectural capacity, and nonlinear performance to flexible inference beyond reproducing a fixed filter.

D1.justification: V2 adds a link to experimental code, detailed buffer/index walkthroughs and transformer-weight constructions. Appendices D–F specify additional prompts, parameter distributions and forecasting procedures; the control-input prompt now explicitly includes B. These substantially expand the information available for reproduction, although some settings remain inconsistent.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of Deep Kalman Filters and attention/state-space connections through Dao and Gu and Sieber et al., plus citations supporting nonlinear tracking and double descent. The original positioning around randomly sampled systems and filtering through ICL remains; Akyürek et al.'s publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The title and much of the existing abstract, introduction, background, experimental narrative and conclusion are rewritten. V2 introduces separate related-work and contribution subsections, divides experimental setup from linear and nonlinear results, and reorganizes and expands the appendices.

P2.justification: Most retained figures are redrawn into paired MSE/MSPD displays with revised styles and legends. Figure 5 adds dimension-specific curves and zoomed insets. New nonlinear, distribution-shift and forecasting figures, together with capacity tables, substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's prediction-difference plots, v2's ground-truth MSE, capacity tests and dimension-dependent robustness qualifications improve validation. However, its new tracking claims rely on comparisons accompanied by an incorrect bearing Jacobian in Appendix F.2 and contradictory SGD reporting in Figure 7. The PDFs cannot establish whether the Jacobian error affected the EKF results, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
